hypothesis: An exact-run append watcher can reduce the legacy flat-to-STOP transition race by creating STOP only after a newly appended venue-backed cohort snapshot proves all four assets flat, order-free, and fault-free.
decision: Arm the watcher from the current ledger EOF for run bidirectional-live-1785826133777 and profile c992cb2f958ed607d25d6be76a52a37070278061c0e8c186723dc574e6938f6b. Normal protected-open snapshots remain pending. Identity mismatch, malformed rows, faults, truncation, or an existing STOP request fail closed. The watcher cannot place, close, size, or route orders.
falsifier: Any historical row triggering STOP, any STOP created while a position or owned order remains, an open snapshot terminating the armed watcher, acceptance of another run or profile, overwrite of an existing STOP request, or a backend re-entry after the qualifying flat snapshot invalidates the watcher or its race-reduction claim.
limitations: The watcher consumes backend venue-backed cohort snapshots rather than making an independent authenticated venue query.
It reduces the legacy race because snapshots are emitted after routing and before the next polling interval, but it is not a formal proof against host scheduling or process failure.
STOP is process control and does not itself reconcile or cancel venue state.
A separate venue-bound checkpoint and exact candidate startup verification remain mandatory after the legacy backend exits.
The active HYPE lifecycle remains controlled by the original in-memory profile until it becomes flat.
